Ibn Tahir with twenty thousand men, and came against Balash.
And he waged a fierce battle against it,
and breached the wall.
And he entered and seized the rebels of Nasr's faction,
and cast them into irons,
and sent them to Baghdad.
Nasr, however, within the borders of Sarug, was killing Christians and Persians.
And in the year 1133
(1133 of the Greeks):
The Romans plotted against him to kill him,
and to set up Michael the commander of the army.
And when Leo perceived this,
he sent and arrested Michael {OCR?: ܡܝܕܐܝܠ for ܡܝܟܐܝܠ},
and prepared to crucify him on Good Friday.
His wife, however, persuaded him that he should not be killed on that day.
Then he—Leo (Michael? [Bedjan's note])—sent word to the leaders:
"If you do not save me,
I will make known that all of you were my accomplices in the plot."
And when the leaders were hard pressed,
they rushed upon the emperor while he was standing in the sanctuary and praying,
and killed him.
And they brought out Michael and made him king.
Four years after this one became king, Thekla his wife died;
and he sent and brought out of a monastery the granddaughter of Constantine, and took her as his wife.
And when she bore him a son,
she became indignant that, being the granddaughter of Empress Irene,
she should raise a child from the race of the Jews.
And she devised a plan and killed her own son.
For the ancestor of this Michael was a Jew,
who had believed and been baptized.
At this time al-Ma'mun summoned Thomas, who said of himself that he was the son of Emperor Constantine,
and sent him with an army against Constantinople.
And he came, struck against it, and besieged it for six months.
And when Emperor Michael was hard pressed,
he promised the Arab prisoners their release if they would fight against Thomas.
And when the Romans went out with the Arabs, they shattered the army that was with Thomas.
And he fled to a certain fortress;
and he was overtaken,
his hands and feet were cut off,
and he was impaled on a spear.
Michael, however, went back on his promise,
and did not release the Arab {OCR?: ܩܛܝܝܐ for ܛܝܝܐ} prisoners.
And in the year 1135,
in Tishrin, Ibn Tahir encamped against Kaysum,
and set up there catapults which hurled stones, each of which was a donkey's load.
Kaysum had five walls and a rampart {OCR?}.
Nasr, however, ordered that the Christian women should go up onto the wall
notes: (821 of our Lord?) when Leo grew oppressive and killed many of the nobles.
